cell.st_moths_tip.note: Statistics box: the moths row's tooltip. {from} is where the lantern list came from (the mod's own list, or the one it ships with).

cell.st_moved_in.note: Statistics box, under references: references a later plugin moved into this cell.

cell.st_no_mesh_record.note: Statistics box, under objects: objects whose record names no mesh. Shown red.

cell.st_npc_markers.note: Statistics box, under corpses: NPC markers.

cell.st_objects.note: Statistics box: how many placed objects the loaded cells hold.

cell.st_overridden.note: Statistics box, under references: references a later plugin replaced.

cell.st_references.note: Statistics box: how many object references the loaded cells hold.

cell.st_textures.note: Statistics box: how many land textures the loaded cells use.

cell.st_triangles_v.note: Statistics box: the triangles row's value.

cell.st_water.note: Statistics box (viewport, Real cell mode): the row for an interior's water.

cell.st_water_nobody.note: Statistics box: the water tooltip's {level} when no plugin set a level.

cell.st_water_none.note: Statistics box: the water row's value when the cell has no water level.

cell.st_water_tip.note: Statistics box: the water row's tooltip — which plugin set the level and which set the flag.

cell.st_water_units.note: Statistics box: the water row's value — the level in game units.

cell.stats_title.note: Viewport, the statistics box: its heading in Real cell mode.

cell.status_choose.note: Left column, Preview: the status line under the cell button before one is chosen.

cell.status_failed.en: {n} failed to load, so the blend at those edges is not what the export will use
cell.status_failed.note: The status line, appended when neighbouring cells would not load.

cell.status_interior.note: The status line, appended after " · " when the loaded cell is an interior.

connect.log_archives.other.en: {n} archives read — {names} — {packed} packed files behind the loose ones

connect.log_cells.note: The connect log: cells and landscapes found.

connect.log_indexed.note: The connect log: the asset index.

connect.log_plugins.note: The report dialogue, the connect log: what was read.

connect.log_refs.note: The connect log: how the plugins' references merged.

connect.log_times.en: read {read} ms · parse {parse} ms · merge {merge} ms · meshes {meshes} ms

dlg.cancel.note: The option that changes nothing, in the second confirmation and the paste dialogue.

eng.mo2_dir_missing.en: ModOrganizer.ini points {key} at {path}, which is not there

eng.mo2_no_profiles.note: An engine error (layout.rs, main.rs): the MO2 folder has no profiles.

eng.mo2_profile_missing.note: A connect warning (layout.rs): the remembered MO2 profile is gone.

eng.no_install.note: An engine error (src-tauri/src/main.rs): a command that needs a setup was called before one was connected.

eng.no_install_is.note: An engine error (src-tauri/src/main.rs): the same, from the export path.

eng.no_interior.note: An engine error (src-tauri/src/main.rs): an interior the load order does not have.

eng.no_meshes_folder.en: no Meshes\ folder here — is this really Data Files?

eng.not_in_load_order.en: not found in the load order: {path}
eng.not_in_load_order.note: An engine error (src-tauri/src/main.rs): a mesh or texture path no root has.

eng.not_mo2_folder.en: {path} does not look like an MO2 folder — expected mods\ and profiles\ inside it
eng.not_mo2_folder.note: An engine error (layout.rs, main.rs): connecting MO2 from the wrong folder.

eng.open_failed.en: could not open {dir} in the file browser: {err}
eng.open_failed.note: An engine error (profiles.rs): the system's file browser would not start for Open folder.

eng.openmw_no_data.note: An engine error (layout.rs): openmw.cfg names no data folder that exists.

eng.order_no_plugins.en: {file} lists no plugins — expected [Game Files] GameFile0=… or content=… lines

eng.pack_exists.en: {file} is already there — choose it in Settings, or give the new one another code

eng.pack_missing_file.note: An engine error (src-tauri/src/main.rs): Refresh this pack found no such file.

eng.pack_no_code.note: An engine error (lang.rs): a language pack whose header has no code.

eng.pack_no_language.en: no [language] table — a pack starts with [language] and its code
eng.pack_no_language.note: An engine error (lang.rs): a language pack without its header.

eng.pack_not_found.note: An engine error (lang.rs): the profile's language pack is not in the language folders.

eng.pack_stray_lt.en: a stray < — write < for a less-than sign
eng.pack_stray_lt.note: A language pack line refused (lang.rs): a < that is not a tag.

eng.pack_tag.en: uses <{tag}>, which the English does not — a pack may use only the tags its English uses
eng.pack_tag.note: A language pack line refused (lang.rs): a tag the English does not use.

legend.hover_slot.note: Viewport legend: the highlight of a hovered grass card.

legend.hover_texture.note: Viewport legend: the highlight of a hovered land texture.

legend.mesh_missing_note.en: a position won and nothing to draw

legend.no_grass.note: Viewport legend: the cull overlay's entry; its note lists the reasons.

legend.painted_grass.note: Viewport legend: the Grass cover colour.

legend.painted_rule.note: Viewport legend: a rule colour's entry.

legend.reserved.note: Viewport legend: the markers for empty and object-id slots.

legend.steeper.note: Viewport legend, the "No grass placed" note: ground over the rule's steepest slope.

legend.wrong_curve.note: Viewport legend, the "No grass placed" note: the curvature band.

legend.wrong_object.en: the wrong distance from an object
legend.wrong_object.note: Viewport legend, the "No grass placed" note: the near-objects band.

legend.wrong_shore.en: the wrong distance from the sea
legend.wrong_shore.note: Viewport legend, the "No grass placed" note: the shoreline band.

name.create.note: The name-it dialogue's confirming button when the caller gives no wording.

name.default_title.note: The name-it dialogue's heading when the caller gives none.

name.taken.en: There is already a rule called that. Both will work — they are told apart by what they are, not by what they are called — but the two will be hard to tell apart in a list.
name.taken.note: The name-it dialogue: the warning under the field when the name is already in use.

paint.n_cells.one.note: Part of a "Cleared … from …" toast: how many cells.

preview.adjacent_title.en: How far out from the chosen cell the landscape and its objects are loaded. More cells is more to read and more to draw.

preview.dof_title.en: Depth of field, as MGE XE's Depth of Field.fx draws it: an eye focused on whatever is at the middle of the screen, with what is nearer or further going soft. The same shader's distance blur in fog runs under the water whether this is on or off, because that is where the fog starts behind the eye. Preview only.

preview.fogd_from.note: Left column, on the sources line after Reset to install — before the file the fog distances came from.

preview.fogd_reset_title.en: Put the haze back to what your install says: MGE XE's own distances for the weather, read from mge3\MGE.ini when you have one.

preview.fogd_title.en: How thick the haze is. 100 is MGE XE's own distance for this weather; less clears the air, more closes it in. Under the water it scales the game's underwater distances the same way, so their ratio stays the install's. Only the atmosphere's fog — the plain backdrop's is not touched.

preview.fxaa_title.en: Fast approximate anti-aliasing over the finished picture - the FXAA shader MGE XE runs last in its chain - on top of the multisampling the preview already has. Smooths the edges the multisampling leaves, at some softness. Preview only.

preview.grassfar_cells.one.note: Left column, Preview: the grass-distance slider's value.

preview.grassfar_cells.other.note: Left column, Preview: the grass-distance slider's value.

preview.grassfar_off.note: Left column, Preview: the grass-distance slider's value at zero.

preview.grassfar_title.en: How far from the camera grass is drawn, in cells. The blades shrink away over the last stretch rather than popping out. Preview only — the plugin still gets every blade. Off draws the lot, which is slow with many cells loaded.

preview.hint.en: Changes only what you see, never the plugin.

preview.hint_title.en: Nothing here reaches the generated plugin — only what you are shown and how it is lit.

preview.hour_title.en: The game hour. Sunrise and sunset are read from your Morrowind.ini, and the sun follows the game's own arc.

preview.lights_title.en: Whether the cell's lamps are lit. Night time is the game hour rule: on from 18:00 to 07:00. A lamp's glass and flame follow its light.

preview.mge_title.en: The blades lit and cut out as MGE XE's grass shader does it: light wrapping round the blade with a little glow from behind, a soft-edged cutout, and the mesh's vertex colours ignored as MGE ignores them. Off draws them by the plain rules the placed objects get.

preview.mgew_title.en: The water as MGE XE's water shader draws it: the sky and the shore reflected, the bottom seen through the shallows, the sun's glint, and MGE's own waves when your install has its water_NRM texture. Off is the plain translucent sheet.

preview.mode_hint_cell.en: The real landscape and every placed object. Slower; the only way to see clipping.
preview.mode_hint_cell.note: Left column, under the mode picker while Real cell is chosen.

preview.mode_hint_simple.en: A synthetic patch: instant, good for judging density and clustering.
preview.mode_hint_simple.note: Left column, under the mode picker while Simplified is chosen.

preview.mode_hint_start.en: Simplified previews a synthetic patch: instant, and enough for judging density and clustering.

preview.particles_title.en: The particle systems the meshes carry — a waterfall's mist, a torch's flame and smoke, a candle's flicker — run as the game runs them. A lamp's follow the Lights rule. Preview only.

preview.renderer_att.en: [LightAttenuation] from {file}: constant {c}, linear {l}, quadratic {q} (a 256-unit lamp: c {c256}, l {l256}, q {q256})
preview.renderer_att.note: Hover text on the sources line — the light attenuation settings read, the file they came from, and the coefficients they give a 256-unit lamp.

preview.renderer_att_default.en: [LightAttenuation] not in {file}: the game's shipped values (linear 3/r)
preview.renderer_att_default.note: Hover text on the sources line — no [LightAttenuation] section was found, so the shipped values are used.

preview.renderer_model_ffp.en: fixed pipeline (per vertex in the game): 1/(c + l·d + q·d²) per lamp, the sum clamped to white.
preview.renderer_model_ffp.note: Hover text on the sources line — what the fixed-pipeline lighting model is (vanilla, MGE with per-pixel lighting off, OpenMW's legacy method).

preview.renderer_model_mge.en: MGE XE per-pixel lighting: 1/(q·d² + c) per lamp, the linear term dropped as its shader drops it; the lit colour tonemapped, not clamped; the grass takes sun and ambient only.
preview.renderer_model_mge.note: Hover text on the sources line — what the MGE lighting model is.

preview.renderer_model_openmw.en: OpenMW shaders: 1/(c + l·d + q·d²) per lamp, capped at 1, faded out between {bounds}× the radius and twice that.
preview.renderer_model_openmw.note: Hover text on the sources line — what the OpenMW shader lighting model is; {bounds} is its light bounds multiplier.

preview.renderer_post.note: Hover text on the sources line — the post-process shaders the install's chain names that the preview has an answer for (SSAO, sunshafts…), or 'none'.

preview.shadows_title.en: The sun's shadows, as MGE XE draws them: two cascades near the camera, softened, fading out with the fog. Cast by the terrain, the placed objects and whatever moves among them, and never by grass - a shadow map cannot resolve a blade, and the game does not cast from grass either. Preview only.

preview.shafts_title.en: MGE XE's sunshafts: rays of the sun's light streaming past whatever stands against the sky, as its Sunshafts.fx shader draws them. Turn to face the sun to see them. Costs a few full-screen passes a frame.

preview.sky_room.en: Off in a room: an interior has no sky unless its cell is flagged to behave like an exterior. Your setting comes back when you leave.
preview.sky_room.note: Left column, the tooltip on the dimmed Atmosphere row while an interior is up.

preview.sky_src.note: Left column, under the Weather picker — the lead-in before the list of files the sky's colours were read from.

preview.sky_src_builtin.en: no weather in the ini, the game's own colours
preview.sky_src_builtin.note: Left column, under the atmosphere rows — the ini or openmw.cfg had no [Weather] blocks.

preview.sky_src_mge2.note: Left column, under the atmosphere rows — fog distances, and the file they were read from (mgeXE.toml or mge3\MGE.ini).

preview.sky_src_mge_default.note: Left column, under the atmosphere rows — no MGE.ini, MGE XE's built-in fog distances.

preview.sky_src_mge_how.en: how the fog file was chosen: {how}
preview.sky_src_mge_how.note: Left column, the title (hover text) on the sources line — why that MGE config file was the one read.

preview.sky_src_none.en: Sky: the game's own colours, until an install is connected.
preview.sky_src_none.note: Left column, under the atmosphere rows while nothing is connected.

preview.sky_src_renderer.note: Left column, under the atmosphere rows — the renderer whose lighting model the preview follows, by its own name (e.g. 'MGE-XE G7 Fork v0.20.0', 'OpenMW', 'Morrowind.exe, no MGE').

preview.sky_title.en: The game's sky, sun and haze for the hour and weather, drawn MGE XE's way. Off is the plain backdrop and the flat fog.

preview.ssao_title.en: Ambient occlusion, from the picture's own depth: where a rock meets the ground, where walls turn and under the eaves, the ambient light is dimmed for the sky those places cannot see. Preview only; costs three full-screen passes a frame.

preview.texdetail_title.en: The largest size a texture is loaded at. Bigger files arrive as their own smaller mip - the same picture, far fewer bytes to move and to keep on the GPU. Full is the file's own size. The game's own textures are 512 or smaller and are never touched.

preview.timeflow_title.en: Let the clock run, so the light changes while you watch. Off, the time of day is only what the slider says.

preview.timescale_title.en: How fast the clock runs: game minutes per real second. The clouds drift at this pace too — 20 is the game's own — whether or not the clock is running.

preview.tint_title.en: How much of the ground's colour a blade takes at its base, fading to its own colour at the tip. Preview only: a placed blade carries no colour.

preview.under_title.en: What the game shows with the eye under the water: its underwater fog, in the install's own colour and distances, the surface seen from beneath, and the wobble and light rays (in a room, the caustics) of MGE XE's Underwater Effects shaders. Off, the frame is drawn as if the eye were in the air. Preview only.

preview.unlit_title.en: Draw every surface at its texture, with no sun, ambient or lamps on it - the colours as they are painted. The fog stays. Preview only.

preview.wind_title.en: How hard the grass sways. Preview only: nothing in the plugin moves. Zero is still.

profiles.no_engine.note: Toast when the profiles dialogue is opened with no engine.

profiles.not_saved.note: The report dialogue: a warning when the profile file could not be written.

profiles.not_saved_read.en: profile not saved — settings could not be read: {err}
profiles.not_saved_read.note: The report dialogue: a warning when the settings could not be gathered for saving.

profiles.start_failed.en: Could not open your profiles — starting from defaults. {err}
profiles.start_failed.note: Toast at start-up when the profile store could not be read.

report.assets_ok.en: Every referenced mesh and texture loaded cleanly.
report.assets_ok.note: Load-order report, under Assets, when nothing was missing.

report.copied.note: Load-order report, what a copy button says for a moment after it has copied.

report.copyall_title.en: Copy the whole report to the clipboard

report.copyfail.en: Could not copy — select the text and copy it by hand
report.copyfail.note: Load-order report, said when the clipboard refused the write.

report.copysec.note: Load-order report, the button on each section heading that copies that section.

report.copysec_title.en: Copy this section to the clipboard

report.copywait.note: The report's copy buttons while a GPU line is still being measured; the copy follows once it is in.

report.index_warnings.en: Could not read while indexing objects: {list}
report.index_warnings.note: Load-order report: the warning box when some object records could not be read; {list} is the reasons.

report.masters.note: Load-order report, under a plugin: its masters; {list} is them, joined by dots.

report.mesh_missing.note: The report dialogue: a mesh the engine could not read.

report.missing_from_bundle.note: A grass card's swatch tooltip: the engine's mesh bundle had no entry for it.

report.missing_plugins.en: {n} plugin(s) listed but not found through the current stack: {list}
report.missing_plugins.note: Load-order report: the warning box for plugins the order names but the install lacks; {list} is up to eight of them.

report.no_geometry.en: {path}: no visible geometry (filler or placeholder mesh)
report.no_geometry.note: The report dialogue: a mesh with nothing to draw.

report.not_a_mesh.en: the engine sent something that is not a mesh
report.not_a_mesh.note: A grass card's swatch tooltip, and the report: the mesh data was not a mesh.

report.not_loaded.note: After a master in that list that the order does not load.

report.order_none.en: No plugin load order found. Looked for the MO2 profile's Morrowind.ini [Game Files], then loadorder.txt / plugins.txt, then Morrowind.ini in Data Files. Texture and region checking stays off until one is found.
report.order_none.note: The report dialogue when no load order was found.

report.order_read.en: Read from {source} — {n} plugin(s), in the order the game loads them. Later entries override earlier ones. This should match MO2's right pane top-to-bottom.
report.order_read.note: The report dialogue: where the load order came from; {source} is bold.

report.tint.note: Load-order report: the ground tint heading.

report.tint_off.en: — off, so nothing below is read by the grass
report.tint_off.note: After that line while the tint is off.

report.tint_slider.note: Load-order report, under Ground tint; {pct} is the slider.

settings.btn_title.note: Top bar: the Settings button's tooltip before the folder is known.

settings.lang_broken_note.note: Settings, Language: the note when the chosen pack file will not parse.

settings.lang_create_failed.en: Could not create the language file: {err}
settings.lang_create_failed.note: Toast when Create new language file failed; {err} is the engine's reason.

settings.lang_create_title.en: Start a translation: a gardenfell.<code>.toml in the languages folder with every string listed, its English above and an empty value to fill in

settings.lang_created.en: Created {file} — every string listed with its English above. Fill it in, then choose it here; Refresh this pack brings it up to date after a new version of Gardenfell.
settings.lang_created.note: Toast after Create new language file.

settings.lang_english.note: Settings, Language: the picker's first entry — the wording built into the program.

settings.lang_missing_note.en: This profile asks for {file}, which is not in that folder — English until it is.
settings.lang_missing_note.note: Settings, Language: the note when the profile's pack is not on this machine.

settings.lang_missing_toast.en: This profile asks for the language pack {file}, which is not in {dir}. English until it is.
settings.lang_missing_toast.note: Toast at start-up (and on switching profile) when the profile names a pack the machine lacks.

settings.lang_new_code_body.en: The language's code, as in BCP 47 — sv, de, pt-BR, zh-Hans. It names the file: gardenfell.<code>.toml.
settings.lang_new_code_body.note: Settings, Language: the first question — the code.

settings.lang_new_head.note: Settings, Language: the title of the two questions Create new language file asks.

settings.lang_new_name_body.en: What the language calls itself — Svenska, Deutsch, Português do Brasil. This is what the picker shows for {file}.
settings.lang_new_name_body.note: Settings, Language: the second question — the name; {file} is the pack file about to be made.

settings.lang_new_next.note: Settings, Language: the button that takes the code and asks for the name.

settings.lang_new_taken.en: A pack with that code is already in the languages folder — choose it in the picker, or pick another code.
settings.lang_new_taken.note: Settings, Language: the warning under the code field when a pack for that code exists.

settings.lang_note.en: Packs are gardenfell.<code>.toml files in {dir} — the languages folder under where your files are kept, so they move with the rest. Drop one there and choose it here; the choice is saved in your profile. Text the program draws as you work catches up as it is redrawn.
settings.lang_note.note: Settings, Language: the note under the picker; {dir} is the languages folder.

settings.lang_open_title.en: Show the languages folder in your file browser

settings.lang_orphans_note.en: {n} of its keys are not in this version of Gardenfell any more — kept in the file, not used. Refresh this pack to sort them to the end.
settings.lang_orphans_note.note: Settings, Language: appended when the pack has keys the catalogue lacks.

settings.lang_pack_broken.note: Settings, Language: a pack file the engine could not read, greyed in the picker.

settings.lang_pack_missing_option.note: Settings, Language: the picker entry for the language the profile asks for when no pack provides it.

settings.lang_pack_note.en: {name} by {author}, made for Gardenfell {madeFor} — {translated} of {total} strings translated; the rest show English.
settings.lang_pack_note.note: Settings, Language: the note describing the chosen pack.

settings.lang_pack_option.note: Settings, Language: a pack in the picker, by its own name, with its coverage.

settings.lang_problem_line.note: Settings, Language: one refused line of the pack — its line number, key and reason.

settings.lang_problems_note.one.note: Settings, Language: the heading over the pack's refused lines (one).

settings.lang_problems_note.other.note: Settings, Language: the heading over the pack's refused lines.

settings.lang_problems_toast.en: {name}: {n} line(s) could not be used — Settings says which.
settings.lang_problems_toast.note: Toast when a pack with refused lines is applied.

settings.lang_reload_title.en: Look in the languages folder again, after dropping a pack in

settings.lang_switched.en: Now speaking {name}. Text the program draws as you work catches up as it is redrawn.
settings.lang_switched.note: Toast after a language pack is chosen.

settings.lang_update_failed.note: Toast when Refresh this pack failed.

settings.lang_update_title.en: Bring the chosen pack up to date with this version of Gardenfell: every translation kept, new strings added empty with their English above, the old file kept under backups

settings.lang_updated.en: Refreshed {file} — {added} new strings added empty, {orphans} no longer used; the old file is kept as {backup}.

settings.language_title.en: The language the program speaks. English is built in; anything else is a pack somebody made and put in the languages folder

settings.nav_hint2.en: Orbit navigation: the left button clicks objects and paints, the right button orbits, middle-drag pans and the wheel zooms. WASD on Right mouse button: hold the right button to look around where you stand and fly with W A S D (E up, Q down), the wheel setting the speed; the left button clicks objects and paints, and never orbits.

settings.open_failed.note: Toast when Open folder or Open languages folder could not start the file browser; {err} is the engine's reason.

settings.sens_title.en: How far the view turns for a given movement of the mouse while the right button is held. The middle is the rate Gardenfell shipped with; the left end a quarter of it, the right end four times. WASD scheme only.

settings.smooth_orbit_rot_title.en: How fast the view catches up with the mouse while you drag the orbit round: the turn lags behind and closes in at this rate. Low is smooth and slow, 100 is nearly direct. Orbit scheme only.

settings.smooth_orbit_title.en: How fast the camera follows a pan or the wheel: the view closes on where you put it at this rate. Low is a soft, gliding move; 100 is instant. Orbit scheme only.

settings.smooth_pos_title.en: How fast the flying camera gets going and stops when a key is pressed or let go: the speed closes on what the keys ask for at this rate. Low is a soft, slow start and stop; 100 is nearly instant. WASD scheme only.

settings.smooth_rot_title.en: How fast the view catches up with the mouse while the right button is held: the turn lags behind and closes in at this rate. Low is smooth and slow, 100 is nearly direct. WASD scheme only.

settings.theme_default.note: Settings, Theme: the palette the program ships with — sage on true grey.

settings.theme_firmament.note: Settings, Theme: a palette — dark greys and starlight, Masser's rust for the warm colours; the quiet one.

settings.theme_hlaalu.note: Settings, Theme: a palette — coin gold on yellow clay.

settings.theme_note.en: The paint colours for Grass and No Grass never change with the theme.

settings.theme_redoran.note: Settings, Theme: a palette — oxide on vellum, the light one.

settings.theme_telvanni.note: Settings, Theme: a palette — spore green on aubergine.

settings.theme_title.en: The colours the window wears. Saved in the profile.

settings.theme_unknown.en: A theme this version has not got
settings.theme_unknown.note: Settings, Theme: the entry for a theme the profile names and this build has no colours for; its code is shown beside it.

settings.theme_velothi.note: Settings, Theme: a palette — ember on ashfall.

toast.show_it.note: A toast's cue line when the caller gives no wording.

top.connected_title.en: Connected — click to connect a different {kind} install
top.connected_title.note: Top bar, the tooltip on the connect button of the install that is live; {kind} is "MO2", "OpenMW" or "Data Files".

top.engine_title.note: Top bar, the tooltip on the folder state; {n} is the engine's thread count.

top.folder_report_title.en: Click for the plugin load order and asset report
top.folder_report_title.note: Top bar: the connected-setup label's tooltip.

top.report_title.en: What was read: the plugin load order with each plugin's masters, the archives opened, the meshes and textures found, and anything that could not be read.

unit.min_s.note: A time in minutes and seconds.

vp.arrows_title.en: Show the four arrows that step the view one cell in each direction

vp.compass_title.en: North, as the camera sees it: the needle points to the game's +Y however the view is turned

vp.cull_both.note: Viewport, the Highlight culling button in its third state.

vp.cull_off.note: Viewport, the Highlight culling button while it is off.

vp.cull_terrain.note: Viewport, the Highlight culling button in its second state.

vp.cull_title.en: Shade what the steepest-slope and ground-height limits are keeping grass off. Click cycles: off, terrain only, terrain and statics.

vp.empty_title.en: Show a marker at every position an empty/placeholder or object-ID slot won

vp.hiobj_outline.note: Viewport, the Highlight objects button in its third state (round 18dq): an outline around the pointed-at object instead of the gold fill.

vp.hiobj_title.en: Pointing at an object in the viewport lights it up, and hovering a never-avoid pattern lights up everything it matches

vp.hislot_title.en: Hovering a grass slot lights up every instance it placed and dims the rest

vp.hitex_title.en: Hovering a ground texture — in the left column or in this cell's list — lights up the ground it covers

vp.nav_title.en: Which way the mouse moves the camera. Orbit: the right button orbits, the left picks and paints. WASD: hold the right button to look and fly with W A S D. Press to swap.

vp.nav_wasd_text.note: Viewport, the navigation button's own words while the WASD scheme is on. The Orbit wording is the button's markup (vp.nav_orbit).

vp.noctx_body.en: The rule editor and .toml export still work — only the viewport is affected.
vp.noctx_body.note: The viewport, under that line, after the browser's own reason.

vp.noctx_title.note: The viewport, the big line when WebGL could not start.

vp.noengine_body.en: This page is the front half of a desktop application. Launch Gardenfell itself — everything here reads and places grass through the engine, and there is nothing behind this window to answer.

vp.noengine_title.en: Gardenfell is not running its engine
vp.noengine_title.note: The viewport when the page is opened in a plain browser: the big line.

vp.orbit_paint2.en: left-drag to paint · right-drag to orbit · middle-drag to pan · wheel to zoom · CTRL+Wheel to move pivot

vp.orbit_pick2.en: click an object · right-drag to orbit · middle-drag to pan · wheel to zoom · CTRL+Wheel to move pivot

vp.orbit_plain2.en: right-drag to orbit · middle-drag to pan · wheel to zoom · CTRL+Wheel to move pivot

vp.recentre_title.en: Point the camera back at the middle of what is loaded

vp.recentred.note: Toast after the recentre-view shortcut puts the camera back.

vp.speed_title.en: Flying speed, units a second — the wheel changes it too

vp.wasd_fly.en: move the mouse to look · W A S D to move · E up · Q down · wheel sets speed · release to stop

vp.wasd_paint.en: left-drag to paint · hold right button + W A S D (E up, Q down) to fly · wheel sets speed

vp.wasd_pick.en: click an object · hold right button + W A S D (E up, Q down) to fly · wheel sets speed

vp.wasd_plain.en: hold right button + W A S D (E up, Q down) to fly · wheel sets speed
